title: Cross-functional Livetrain for Rollouts and Microexperiments (Sandbox)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sandbox for a "livetrain" pattern that structures cross-functional rollout activity as a continuous, timeboxed cadence. The goal is to move away from ad hoc canaries toward a predictable, rehearsed sequence of microexperiments and safety rehearsals that teams can join and interoperate with.

Scope and intent:
- Focus: LLM feature rollouts, hybrid inference routing changes, and small A/B experiments tied to model variants and routing policies.
- Not in scope: large monolithic migrations (these get a separate program).
- Intended audience: product PMs, release stewards, SRE/ops oncall, solutions eng, privacy/compliance reviewers, and customer success for enterprise-impacting rollouts.

Definitions (quick):
- Livetrain: a recurring cadence (weekly or biweekly) that runs multiple short-lived microexperiments, health rehearsals, and slice-specific canaries in a single orchestrated window.
- Bridge Cohort: a transitional cohort that receives mirrored traffic plus a small weighted active allocation to validate downstream behavior under realistic load.
- Mirror-burst: short high-fidelity mirrored traffic run used to validate latencies and KV cache behavior without user-visible exposure.
- Silent-scan: low-impact synthetic probing traffic that surfaces content and hallucination signals without affecting end users.

Roles and responsibilities (practical):
- Livetrain Conductor (product steward): owns cadence schedule, participant roster, and cross-team announcements.
- Release Operator (ops/SRE): manages traffic routing toggles, throttles, emergency cutoff, and automations for rollback.
- Experiment Owner (feature PM/eng): supplies hypothesis, signal definitions, and retrospective notes.
- Measurement Lead (observability): guarantees dashboards, query owners, and signal SLAs are available pre-window.
- Safety Reviewer (policy/moderation/security): quick-scan signoff; can veto or require mitigations.

Livetrain cadence (example weekly template):
- T-5 days: Hypothesis & checklist submitted to livetrain board (template below). Attach sample prompts, safety tags, and expected cardinality.
- T-3 days: Measurement smoke tests — observability runs mirror-burst and silent-scan; metric queries validated.
- T-1 day: Final readiness sync (15 minutes) between conductor, release operator, measurement lead.
- Window day (2–4 hours):
  - Phase 0 (15m): Mirror-burst / silent-scan baseline (no exposed traffic). Verify KV cache, tail latency, memory growth.
  - Phase 1 (30–60m): Bridge Cohort live allocation 0.1%–1% with strict latency budget gating.
  - Phase 2 (30–90m): Incremental ramp by doubling slices if signal OK (max 5%).
  - Phase 3 (continuous observation): Maintain allocation for minimal useful sample (stat power) then re-evaluate for extended A/B.

Design patterns (novel sketches):
- Bridge Cohort: useful for routing changes where cache-warmth and per-customer personalization matter. Mirror traffic into a shadow instance while routing a small fraction of live users. Use deterministic user hashing to bind repeated exposures for signal consistency.
- Mirror-burst then Activate: mirror first, run a burst (higher synthetic concurrency) to detect kernel/backpressure regressions, then enable Bridge Cohort.
- Silent-scan + Active A/B: While 100% synthetic probing runs, roll a tiny active A/B group that only receives lightweight responses (no side-effects) to capture interaction patterns.

Signal gating heuristics (examples you can copy):
- Latency: p95 increase > 20% or absolute p95 > target -> immediate revert.
- Error rate: 5xx spike > 0.5% above baseline sustained for 3 minutes -> auto-cutoff.
- Quality drift: A/B quality metric (eval set score or human RPS) drops below threshold -> stall and auto-rollback.
- Safety hits: content moderation rule violation count > 0.01% -> pause and require manual safety review.
- Cost/Unit: token cost per request > baseline + X% for 30m -> alert but optional gating.

Telemetry checklist (pre-window):
- Route-level p50/p95/p99 for affected model variants.
- Token counts and billing projection for window.
- KV cache hit rate and median cold start time.
- Signal scrapers for hallucination keywords, toxic content classifier outputs.
- User cohort retention of identifiers for consistent sampling.

Runbook (quick ops play):
- Abort (manual): release operator flips the route to baseline prefix + ensures fallback variant pinned. Notify conductor and oncall.
- Auto-cutoff: automated runbook triggers when circuit broken (see gating). The system posts to #rollouts and opens RED-xxxxx incident.
- Fast rollback: prefer rollback to partial mitigation. Reintroduce previously stable model variant and engage postmortem.

Retrospective template (post-window):
- Window summary (who, when, what changed).
- Signals observed vs. expected (attach queries and charts).
- Decisions taken during window (manual cutoffs, throttles).
- Lessons & low-hanging improvements (observability gaps, checklist misses).
- Action items with owners and due dates.

Small experiment checklist (submitter form, keep short):
1) Hypothesis (one sentence).
2) Primary signal & backup signal (metric names and owners).
3) Safety tags (PHI, regulated, moderation).
4) Estimated traffic weight, expected duration.
5) Rollback plan and threshold values.
6) Measurement queries and dashboards (links).

Open design questions / areas for follow-up:
- How to quantify quality drift for non-deterministic LLM outputs without excessive labeling cost? (priority: research + measurement tooling).
- Should the livetrain include a dedicated human-in-the-loop cadence for high-risk customers? (ops + CS to prototype).
- Automating Bridge Cohort creation and teardown as a self-service API for experiment owners.

Operational notes & pragmatic constraints observed in pilots:
- Mirror traffic exposes infra issues that small active cohorts do not (cache, memory, compaction). Always run mirror-burst first.
- Small cohorts need deterministic user mapping to produce signal; random sampling adds noise.
- Observability gaps are most often in derived quality metrics; plan for light-weight human labeling or quick heuristics.

Next steps (near-term):
- Pilot two livetrain windows with paid customers (Prod A and Beta B) in April.
- Build a "livetrain board" template (Conductor) with fields from the small experiment checklist.
- Add automated gating scripts to routing infra: one-click abort and cohort shrink.

Appendix: quick templates and commands (copyable)
- Conductor board template link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROLL-bridge-livetrain
- Quick ops command: /rollout-cutoff --route <route> --reason "livetrain-cutoff"
- Minimal measurement query: SELECT avg(latency_ms) FROM traces WHERE route = '<route>' AND model = '<model>' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep the name "livetrain" intentionally odd — makes the cadence easier to search and reduces accidental misuse.
- Track privacy-sensitive rollouts separately; add mandatory privacy checklist item.

If you want to run a pilot, ping me (Maya) with the hypothesis + one chart and I will slot it into the next livetrain window.
